extracted.intended_audience: researchers/authors submitting manuscripts to Cell Discovery (molecular & cell biology)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for preparing and submitting manuscripts to the open‑access journal Cell Discovery (Springer Nature) including article types, formatting, data and image standards, editorial policies, and post-acceptance procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aims and scope / acceptance standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Cell Discovery publishes results of significance and originality in all areas of molecular & cell biology; the basic bar of acceptance is comparable to prestigious society journals in the respective field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journal is a fully open access international journal; submissions should meet standards of significance and originality appropriate to high-profile molecular cell biology journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article types and associated length/limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines permitted article types (Article, Correspondence, Editorial, Review Article) and gives indicative word limits, abstract limits, and limits on figures/tables/references per type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Article 6,000–8,000 words excl. abstract/references/figures/tables; Correspondence 1,200 words excl.; Review Article up to 15,000 words; unstructured abstracts max 250 words; limits on figures/tables/references provided as guidance — editors may accept exceptions during peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required manuscript components and order
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles must contain the following components in the order stated: Title page, Abstract, Introduction, Results, Discussion, Materials and methods, Acknowledgements, Conflict of interests, Contributions, References, Figure legends, Tables, Figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All textual content should be in a single file (Word or TeX/LaTeX); footnotes are not allowed and should be incorporated parenthetically; follow the specified order to avoid delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover letter requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Each manuscript must be accompanied by a cover letter including specific statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cover letter must include: a Highlight of the manuscript limited to no more than 2 short sentences; confirmation that all authors agree with submission; confirmation that the work has not been published or submitted elsewhere (in any form or language); evidence of permission from copyright holder for reproduced material; a Conflict of Interest Statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title page contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Title page must include succinct title (<200 characters), concise running title (normally ≤50 characters), full names of all authors (given names), affiliations (including city, state if USA, country, zip code), official email addresses of all authors, and full contact details (telephone and fax) of the corresponding author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corresponding author should be identified with an asterisk; provide accurate contact info to avoid delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A brief, unstructured abstract (maximum 250 words) should state the purpose, basic procedures, main findings and principal conclusions of the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstract should not contain abbreviations or references and should not be structured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Introduction should summarize the rationale for the study and outline pertinent background material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Introduction should not contain results or conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results section guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Results should be presented in a logical sequence in the text, tables and figures; repetitive presentation of the same data in different forms should be avoided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Results should not include material appropriate to the Discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion section guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion should not reiterate Results but should consider them in relation to hypotheses in the Introduction and place new information in the context of the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discussion may include advanced evaluation of methodology and relationships of new information to existing knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materials and Methods reproducibility standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Materials and Methods should be described in sufficient detail to allow the experimental work to be reproduced in another laboratory, leaving the reader in no doubt how results were derived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include detailed protocols, reagents, equipment, software and settings where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data availability (Springer Nature Data Policy Type 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission implies that materials described in the manuscript, including all relevant raw data, will be freely available to any researcher for non-commercial purposes, without breaching participant confidentiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Data Availability Statement must be included as part of the manuscript; adhere to the journal's Data Availability Statement guidance and ensure raw data are available upon reasonable request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence and structure deposition requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers reporting protein or DNA sequences and molecular structures will not be accepted without an accession number to a public database (GenBank, EMBL, DDBJ, Uniprot, PDB, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors describing macromolecular structures must provide experimental data upon Editor request if not already in a public database such as PDB, BMRB or Nucleic Acid Database.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgements content restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should acknowledge sources of financial grants and other funding, and declare any industrial links or affiliations; contribution of colleagues or institutions should be acknowledged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include personal thanks or thanks to anonymous reviewers in Acknowledgements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest statement
rubrics_metrics.description: A conflict of interest statement must be included for each contributing author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the Conflict of Interest guidelines in the Editorial Policies section for what constitutes a conflict; declare competing financial interests and other potential conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: References formatting and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: References should follow Nature style: appear as superscript numbers starting at 1 in the text and listed in numerical order at the end, with required bibliographic detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All authors listed for up to five authors; for more than five list first author then et al.; provide first and last page numbers; identify abstracts as such; include preprints and datasets where applicable; use Index Medicus abbreviations for medical journal titles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures — general presentation and accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Use distinct colours with comparable visibility and consider colour‑blind individuals; avoid red/green contrast and the rainbow colour scale; use solid fills and avoid hatch patterns and background shading; label figure parts with lower-case bold 'a', 'b', etc.; axis/key labels in sentence case; units with space after number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure unusual units or abbreviations are spelled out or defined in legend; commas for thousands; prepare figures to be accessible and interpretable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure file preparation and formats (final submission)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each figure saved as separate file; multi-part figures saved as single file (e.g. Figure1a-c); figure number placed above each figure; figure legends inserted in the article text file; images saved in RGB at 300 dpi or higher; preferred vector formats and acceptable bitmap formats listed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferred editable vector formats: .ai, .eps, .pdf, .ps, .svg; layered .psd or .tiff for layered art; .psd, .tif, .jpeg or .png for bitmap images; .ppt if fully editable without styling effects; ChemDraw (.cdx) for chemical structures; use consistent typeface (Arial, Helvetica or Times New Roman) and symbol fonts for Greek letters; prepare figures at expected print size (optimum font 8 pt, no lines thinner than 0.25 pt).

rubrics_metrics.name: Artwork guidelines — image sizes and formats for initial submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendations for converting figures to JPEG before making PDFs; specific pixel widths and resolutions for single and multi-part images for online submission guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Single images width 500 pixels at 125 dpi (JPEG for photos, GIF for line drawings/charts); multi-part images width 900 pixels at 125 dpi; filenaming with .jpg or .gif extension recommended to ensure compatibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Black & white image requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Images must be scanned at a minimum of 300 dpi at publication size; resolution must be maintained during manipulation; images may be rotated or scaled uniformly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjustments to contrast/brightness must be uniform across the image and must not result in loss of any feature, band or spot; removed lanes or joined parts must be indicated with a line; black borders should correspond to image cuts; indicate molecular weights or DNA fragment sizes for gels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphs, histograms and statistics presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Error bars must be described in the figure legend; axes on graphs should extend to zero except for log axes; statistical analyses (including error bars and p values) should only be shown for independently repeated experiments and not for replicates of a single experiment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State number of times an experiment was repeated (N) in the legend; avoid misleading presentation of replicates as independent repeats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables — labeling and content consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables should be labelled sequentially (Table 1, Table 2, etc.), each titled and cited in the text; tables should consist of at least two columns with headings and should not duplicate text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Arabic numerals for table footnotes; ensure data in tables match values cited in text, totals add up, and percentages are calculated correctly; tables may be embedded in the main manuscript file or provided as separate files; obtain permission for previously published tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: House style requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Various stylistic and formatting rules for submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not make rules thinner than 1 pt (0.36 mm); use coarse hatching rather than shading for tints in graphs; color should be distinct when used as identifying tool; use SI units throughout; use commas to separate thousands; abbreviations should be spelled out at first instance and not used for terms used fewer than 4 times; text double-spaced with wide margins; use common word-processing package (e.g., MS Word); embed tables converted into images at end of Word doc or supply as separate file; raw data may be submitted in Excel or tab/comma delimited format; at first mention of a manufacturer include town, (state if USA) and country; all pages and lines must be numbered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary information — purpose and submission rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplementary information is peer-reviewed material directly relevant to article conclusions that cannot fit in print; the article must be complete and self-explanatory without the supplementary information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplementary information must be supplied in its FINAL form for peer review and cannot be altered after acceptance; include a read-me file with brief instructions for viewing files; supply a text summary (no more than 50 words) describing contents of each file and identify file formats; supplementary files are posted on the journal website and linked to the article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary information file restrictions and recommended specs
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on acceptable file formats, file sizes, number of files and technical specs for supplementary materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepted formats include QuickTime (.mov), HTML, MPEG (.mpg), JPEG (.jpg), WAV (.wav), Plain ASCII (.txt), PDF (.pdf), MS Word (.doc), Postscript (.ps), Excel (.xls), TeX/LaTeX (.tex). Number of files should be limited to eight, total file size should not exceed 8 MB, individual files not exceed 1 MB unless cleared with Editorial Office; recommended maximum frame size for movies 480 x 360 pixels at 15 fps; recommended max data rate 150 KB/s and 256-colour palette for images if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language quality and editing
rubrics_metrics.description: English must be of sufficient quality for editors and reviewers to assess the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are advised to have a native English speaker review the manuscript or use a professional language editing service (Nature Research Editing Service, American Journal Experts). Use of language editing is not required and does not guarantee peer review or acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-acceptance administrative requirements (APC & Licence to Publish)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon acceptance the corresponding author will be sent a link to complete the Article Processing Charge payment form and the open access Licence to Publish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forms must be completed promptly to avoid publication delays; government employees in US/UK must complete relevant government open access licence forms; whitelist @springernature.com to ensure receipt of acceptance emails if unavailable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open access license and copyright
rubrics_metrics.description: Open access articles are published under a CC BY licence (Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International); authors retain copyright in their work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CC BY allows users to share and adapt the contribution (including for commercial purposes) provided attribution is given; authors should check funder mandates for required licence types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof correction timeline and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Corresponding author receives an email linking to proofing site; proof corrections must be returned within 48 hours of receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensive changes cannot be made at proof stage; corresponding author is responsible for circulating proofs to co-authors and coordinating corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-archiving policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are encouraged to submit the final accepted peer-reviewed manuscript to their funding body's archive and/or institutional repository immediately upon publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should cite the publication reference and DOI on any deposited version and provide a link to the published article on nature.com.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online submission and pre-submission enquiries
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts must be submitted via the online submission system (or via email for pre-submission enquiries); authors should register for an account to monitor manuscript status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult Editorial Policies and Submission Instructions before submission; submissions only accepted through online system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of revised manuscripts — required materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors submitting a revised manuscript must include (1) a rebuttal letter indicating point-by-point how reviewer comments were addressed; (2) a marked-up version highlighting changes made in response to reviewer comments; (3) a 'clean' non-highlighted version of the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If disagreeing with reviewer points provide adequate justification in the rebuttal letter to aid editor decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article Processing Charge (APC) waiver policy
rubrics_metrics.description: APC waivers available for corresponding authors based in the world's lowest income countries as defined by the World Bank; discretionary waivers considered case-by-case for financial need.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications for discretionary waivers should be made at point of manuscript submission to apcwaivers@springernature.com; editorial decisions are based on editorial criteria and editors/reviewers do not see authors' ability to pay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Each author is expected to have made substantial contributions to conception or design; acquisition, analysis or interpretation of data; creation of new software used in the work; or drafting/substantively revising the work; AND to have approved the submitted version; AND to agree to be personally accountable for their contributions and ensure issues are investigated and resolved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contributors who do not meet all criteria should be noted in Acknowledgements; medical writers and industry employees can be contributors but their roles, affiliations and competing interests must be included; signed statements from medical writers/editors declaring permission to be named are required; failing to acknowledge contributors can be considered inappropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Large Language Models (LLMs) usage and authorship
rubrics_metrics.description: LLMs such as ChatGPT do not currently satisfy authorship criteria and therefore should not be listed as authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of an LLM should be properly documented in the Methods section (or suitable alternative part of the manuscript) describing how the LLM was used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changes to authorship policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Corresponding author is responsible for ensuring correct author list; any changes to author list (addition/removal) between initial submission and acceptance require written agreement from all authors and confirmation that new authors meet authorship requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changes to authorship are not allowed after the manuscript has been accepted for publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence responsibilities of corresponding author
rubrics_metrics.description: The corresponding author is responsible for communicating with the journal, managing communication among co-authors, informing co-authors of matters arising, ensuring author list and order are agreed, and circulating proofs to all co-authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corresponding author is responsible for accuracy of proof content, correct spelling of co-author names, and current addresses/affiliations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and anonymity of peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors, authors and reviewers must keep all details of the editorial and peer review process confidential; peer review is confidential and conducted anonymously unless open peer review declared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must not redistribute manuscripts or data; if a reviewer asks a colleague to assist confidentiality must be ensured and colleague's name provided to the journal; reviewers should not identify themselves to authors without editor's knowledge; policy is to neither confirm nor deny speculation about reviewer identities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media communication restriction during submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Material submitted must not be discussed with the media during consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal reserves the right to halt consideration or publication if this condition is broken.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate publication and preprint policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers must be original and not published or submitted elsewhere in any language; prior publication on recognized community preprint servers is allowed (details and accession numbers must be included in the cover letter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy does not cover preprints publicized to media or otherwise publicized outside the scientific community during submission; meeting abstracts are allowed to be published prior to full contribution but should be included with submission and referred to in cover letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism detection and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Plagiarism and duplicate publication (self-plagiarism) are prohibited; Similarity Check (CrossCheck) is used to screen submissions for overlapping and similar text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors judge cases on their merits; if plagiarism is proven, the journal may contact the author's institute and funding agencies, retract or correct the paper as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data fabrication and falsification policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Falsification (altering data to give a false impression) and fabrication (inventing data) are serious ethical issues; some image manipulation for readability is allowed only when applied to complete images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should notify Editor in cover letter of any technical manipulation; improper manipulations (obscuring, enhancing, deleting or introducing elements) are not allowed and may trigger investigation and corrective action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image integrity and standards (detailed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Images should be minimally processed; authors must retain unprocessed data/metadata; certain image processing is acceptable only if final image correctly represents original data and conforms to community standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should list image acquisition tools and processing software and document key settings/manipulations in Methods; do not combine images from different times/locations unless stated and demarcated; avoid touch-up tools (cloning/healing); processing (brightness/contrast) appropriate only when applied equally across entire image and to controls; excessive manipulations (biased thresholds) are inappropriate; for gels/blots include positive/negative controls and markers, indicate cropping in legends, retain important bands (cropped blots should retain at least six band widths above and below the band), loading controls must be on same blot, avoid quantitative comparisons across different gels unless processed in parallel and described; microscopy adjustments must be applied to entire image; disclose pseudo-colouring and nonlinear adjustments; include equipment details, measured resolution, LUT/lookup table mapping when using pseudo-colours, and name processing software and manipulations (deconvolution, 3D reconstructions, gamma changes, filtering, thresholding, projections).

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction and retraction categories & procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Five categories of amendments: Erratum (publisher correction), Corrigendum (author correction), Retraction, Addendum (including Editorial Expression of Concern), and Editor's Note.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All corrections requests submitted to editorial office; decisions made by Editor sometimes with peer-reviewers' advice; corrections that do not affect scientific understanding (e.g., spelling) are not considered; in misconduct cases investigation follows COPE guidelines, possible outcomes include rejection if under consideration, correction or retraction if published, and informing author's institution or funder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review model and decision outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Journal operates single-blind peer review; manuscripts sent for review are evaluated by at least one independent reviewer (often two or more); editors decide whether to send for external review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial decisions include: Accept (with or without editorial revisions), Revise (authors address reviewer concerns), Reject with potential for resubmission after further work, or Reject outright (insufficient novelty, specialist interest, or major technical/interpretational problems). Only papers likely to meet editorial criteria are sent for external review to expedite process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting peer reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer selection based on expertise, reputation and specific recommendations; authors may suggest reviewers and request exclusion of individuals or laboratories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choice of reviewers is at editors' discretion; reviewers may decline if perceived conflict of interest exists; if a reviewer uses a colleague to assist confidentiality must be preserved and the colleague named to the journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may appeal a rejection decision only once and only after peer review; appeals are considered but take second place to normal workload and often take several weeks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals are successful only if the editors are convinced the original decision was a serious mistake (not a borderline call); substantial errors of fact or evidence of bias by a referee that would have changed the outcome may justify reversal; editors may obtain further referee advice or send responses/revised paper to referees.
